claims.claim: Fredric Jameson argues that The Left Hand of Darkness is built from heterogeneous narrative modes superposed into what amounts to an anthology of narrative strands.
claims.source: Fredric Jameson, 'World Reduction in Le Guin: The Emergence of Utopian Narrative', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: a virtual anthology of narrative strands of different kinds

claims.claim: Jameson says readers are struck by descriptive details such as the cornerstone ceremony and the spring caravan, in which contradictory elements of the real world are recombined into piquant montages.
claims.source: Fredric Jameson, 'World Reduction in Le Guin', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: juxtaposed and recombined into piquant montages
claims.page: section on details suggesting an attempt to reimagine history

claims.claim: Darko Suvin calls Le Guin a classical writer whose energy is strictly controlled within a taut and spare architectural system of narrative cells.
claims.source: Darko Suvin, 'Parables of De-Alienation: Le Guin's Widdershins Dance', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975), abstract as printed on the SFS page
claims.quote: a taut and spare architectural system of narrative cells

claims.claim: Suvin judges the Earthsea trilogy Le Guin's best work up to The Dispossessed when seen from a purely formal viewpoint of internal consistency and stylistic clarity.
claims.source: Darko Suvin, 'Parables of De-Alienation', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: internal consistency and stylistic clarity, that trilogy is

claims.claim: Suvin describes Le Guin as austerely, almost puritanically, operating a retrenchment throughout her work.
claims.source: Darko Suvin, 'Parables of De-Alienation', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.page: section on Le Guin's ideology and world-reduction

claims.claim: Donald F. Theall argues that because LHD's narrator is a professional cultural analyst concerned with a thorough account of the culture, the novel takes on the characteristic features of an anthropological report.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: the characteristic features of an anthropological report
claims.page: second section, on the stranger visiting a new world

claims.claim: Theall argues that the outsider's separateness makes him observer as well as participant and so allows Le Guin a particularly descriptive approach.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: allows for the particularly descriptive approach
claims.page: second section, on the stranger visiting a new world

claims.claim: Theall says the sensory experience and subjective response of Le Guin's outsiders validates the carefully chosen and believable details that compose her accounts of her worlds.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: the carefully chosen and believable details
claims.page: second section, on the stranger visiting a new world

claims.claim: Theall lists physical geography, sexual customs, cultural evolution, ideology and life-style as the categories of detail through which readers learn Le Guin's two worlds in The Dispossessed.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: details of physical geography, sexual customs, cultural evolution, ideology

claims.claim: Theall quotes LHD's narrator declaring that he will make his report as if he told a story.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall quoting The Left Hand of Darkness §1, in Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: I'll make my report as if I told a story
claims.page: block quotation in the second section

claims.claim: Theall links a Puritan or Yankee tradition to Le Guin's sensibility as it shows in descriptions of the rigors of Karhide and the asceticism of Anarres.
claims.source: Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975), note 1
claims.quote: the rigors of Karhide or the asceticism of Anarres

claims.claim: Bierman disputes that Le Guin is a plain storyteller, saying she is rarely a simple, straightforward one.
claims.source: Judah Bierman, 'Ambiguity in Utopia: The Dispossessed', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: Le Guin is rarely a simple, straightforward storyteller
claims.page: section following the discussion of the ansible

claims.claim: John Huntington says Karhide's feudal monarchy is realised with a care for the way politics works in that archaic system which is new to Le Guin.
claims.source: John Huntington, 'Public and Private Imperatives in Le Guin's Novels', Science Fiction Studies #7 (November 1975)
claims.quote: a care for the way politics works in this

claims.claim: David Mitchell states that Le Guin avoids wide variations of tone or register in A Wizard of Earthsea.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: Le Guin eschews wide variations of tone or register

claims.claim: David Mitchell characterises the narrating voice of Ged’s story as having the calm authority of an age-old Icelandic saga.
claims.source: David Mitchell, "David Mitchell on Earthsea: a rival to Tolkien and George RR Martin", The Guardian, 23 October 2015
claims.quote: the calm authority of an age-old Icelandic saga

verdicts.trueWording: a virtual anthology of narrative strands of different kinds
verdicts.note: Raw curl fetch of the Wayback id_ capture, HTTP 200; page header confirms Jameson, SFS #7, Vol 2 Part 3, November 1975. Opening paragraph: the novel 'can be shown to be constructed from a heterogeneous group of narrative modes artfully superposed and intertwined, thereby constituting' the quoted phrase. Every limb (heterogeneous narrative modes / superposed / anthology of strands) is on the page; the following sentence enumerates the strands (travel narrative, pastiche of myth, political novel, straight SF, Orwellian dystopia, adventure-story, love-story).

verdicts.trueWording: juxtaposed and recombined into piquant montages
verdicts.note: Same raw Jameson capture (one fetch served indices 388 and 391). The passage on details 'suggesting an attempt to reimagine history' asks 'What reader has not indeed been struck' by the opening cornerstone ceremony and the departure of the first spring caravan, then says extrapolation designates 'just such details as these, in which heterogenous or contradictory elements of the empirical real world are' + the quote. Reader-struck limb, both named details, and the recombination limb are all present.

verdicts.trueWording: a taut and spare architectural system of narrative cells
verdicts.note: Raw curl fetch of the Wayback id_ capture, HTTP 200; header confirms Darko Suvin, 'Parables of De-Alienation: Le Guin's Widdershins Dance', SFS #7, November 1975. The ABSTRACT printed at the foot of the page (after the notes) reads: Le Guin is a 'classical' writer, 'her energy is as fierce but is strictly controlled within' + the quote. Claim drops the page's scare quotes around classical and the 'as fierce but' contrast, neither of which it contradicts.

verdicts.trueWording: internal consistency and stylistic clarity, that trilogy is her best
verdicts.note: Same raw Suvin capture. Body, in the Earthsea passage: 'Seen from a purely formal viewpoint of' + the quoted words + 'work up to TD.' TD is the issue-wide abbreviation for The Dispossessed (Suvin uses it 14 times and discusses the novel at length; Theall's article in the same issue defines it explicitly), so the 'up to The Dispossessed' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: the retrenchment she austerely--almost puritanically--operates in all of her work
verdicts.note: Same raw Suvin capture. In the section on Le Guin's ideology and world-reduction: her lonely heretics' position explains 'not only the clear-eyed elegiac atmosphere of Le Guin's, but also' + the quoted words + ', culminating in TD.' Austerity, the near-puritanical qualifier, the retrenchment and its extent across all her work are all on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: provides the novel with the characteristic features of an anthropological report
verdicts.note: Raw curl fetch of the Wayback id_ capture, HTTP 200; header confirms Donald F. Theall, 'The Art of Social-Science Fiction: The Ambiguous Utopian Dialectics of Ursula K. Le Guin', SFS #7, November 1975. One fetch served indices 400-405. In the section on the stranger visiting a new world: in LHD the stranger 'who is also the main narrator--is a professional cultural analyst and cultural communicator, whose concern with a thorough account of the culture' + the quoted words. Causal 'because' limb matches the page's 'whose concern... provides'.

verdicts.trueWording: allows for the particularly descriptive approach
verdicts.note: Same raw Theall capture. Full sentence: 'In each case the separateness of the outsider makes him an observer as well as a participant, and' + the quote. The 'allows Le Guin' limb is supported by the immediate context, which is explicitly about the accounts 'Le Guin gives us of her fictional worlds' and her conscious development of the stranger's role; the page's own wording leaves the beneficiary implicit.

verdicts.trueWording: validating the carefully chosen and believable details which compose the thorough
verdicts.note: Same raw Theall capture. 'The actual sensory experience and subjective response of strangers or outsiders plays a central role in' + the quoted words + 'accounts Le Guin gives us of her fictional worlds.' The claim's 'validates' compresses the page's 'plays a central role in validating', a shade stronger but not a distinct limb.

verdicts.trueWording: details of physical geography, sexual customs, cultural evolution, ideology, life-style
verdicts.note: Same raw Theall capture. In the TD discussion: 'we learn about the' + the quoted words + ', and the like on the two worlds', with the preceding sentences establishing Urras and Anarres and The Dispossessed. All five named categories, the two worlds and the reader-learning limb are present; the page's open-ended 'and the like' means the list is illustrative, which the claim does not deny.

verdicts.trueWording: I'll make my report as if I told a story
verdicts.note: Same raw Theall capture. Theall block-quotes the passage and attributes it '(LHD §1)': the narrator continues 'for I was taught as a child on my hornew[or]ld that Truth is a matter of imagination.' Both limbs -- that Theall quotes it, and that LHD's narrator declares it -- are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: the rigors of Karhide or the asceticism of Anarres
verdicts.note: Same raw Theall capture, endnote 1 (the passage is immediately followed by note 2 citing Le Guin's 'Is Gender Necessary?'). 'There would appear to be a strong though again ambiguous connection between such a Puritan or Yankee tradition and Le Guin's sensibility, which manifests itself in descriptions such as those of' + the quote. The claim's 'links' drops Theall's hedge ('would appear', 'ambiguous'), but the connection is drawn.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin is rarely a simple, straightforward storyteller
verdicts.note: Raw curl fetch of the Wayback id_ capture, HTTP 200; header confirms Judah Bierman, 'Ambiguity in Utopia: The Dispossessed', SFS #7, November 1975. The sentence stands verbatim in the paragraph following the ansible discussion, after 'Ambiguity... is not intended as a euphemism for legitimated confusion', and is followed by 'TD is a complex utopian tale in which she violates the "unities."' Bierman asserts this flatly rather than rebutting a named critic, but asserting it is disputing her plainness.

verdicts.trueWording: a care for the way politics works in this archaic system
verdicts.note: Raw curl fetch of the Wayback id_ capture, HTTP 200; header confirms John Huntington, 'Public and Private Imperatives in Le Guin's Novels', SFS #7, November 1975. In the section on LHD's political structures: 'Though Karhide's feudal monarchy owes a good deal to literary convention, it is realized with a detail and with' + the quoted words + 'which is new to Le Guin.' Claim renders the page's 'this' as 'that' and omits the literary-convention concession, neither of which it contradicts.

verdicts.trueWording: Le Guin eschews wide variations of tone or register
verdicts.note: Live theguardian.com fetched raw with a browser user agent, HTTP 200, full article body present (no Wayback needed despite the robots.txt bar on named agents). Embedded metadata confirms author David Mitchell and datePublished 2015-10-23. Style-and-voice passage: 'Earthsea's accents and dialects are referred to but not reproduced on the page, and' + the quote; the next sentence names A Wizard of Earthsea, so the novel limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: the calm authority of an age-old Icelandic saga
verdicts.note: Same raw Guardian fetch (one fetch served indices 417 and 419). In the style-and-voice section, after the Scylla-and-Charybdis framing: 'Ged's story is told with' + the quote + ', yet stitched here and there with passages of pure beauty for its own sake.' The narrating-voice limb is the page's own 'is told with', within a passage headed by 'Style and voice'.
